newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM gold trails New York lower, PGM ends mixed.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM gold trails New York lower, PGM ends mixed.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended lower across the board on Wednesday after spot gold hovered near fresh four-year lows overnight, while platinum group metals (PGM ) settled mixed, traders said.
The yen's stronger tendency against the dollar also put downward pressure on the market, especially gold futures, they said.

June spot gold expired down 14 yen at noon at 1,233 yen, with 1,553 lots of deliveries. Benchmark April was off 14 yen at 1,229 yen. Spot gold was quoted at $337.80/8.10 at 0717 GMT, against $337.50/338.00 in New York on Tuesday.
"Sentiment toward the gold market remains bearish, although some bargain-hunting buying in gold futures partly offset price losses," one trader said.

Traders said gold futures had more room to dip amid a view that the yen will continue to be strong against the dollar. The dollar dived against the yen in Tokyo on Wednesday, supported by a strong improvement in business sentiment shown in the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey.
In palladium futures, near-term tight supplies and short-covering meant the spot June contract expired at high prices, while distant months were pressured by fresh selling.
The spot June palladium contract expired at noon, up 11 yen per gram at 800 yen, with 116 lots of deliveries.
Benchmark April palladium was flat at 507 yen.

In platinum futures, a slip in spot platinum prices sent nearby months sharply lower, but a expectation that the backwardation would be narrowed after Russia resumes PGM exports, prompted investors to buy platinum distant months.

The June spot contract expired down 39 yen at 1,486 yen. Deliveries were 1,114 lots. Benchmark April platinum was up 10 yen at 1,365 yen. Benchmark April silver was off 1.6 yen per 10 grams at 177.0 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk
